content.value_statement: Agents lose continuity when important context disappears between sessions. This skill helps design vector, graph, and temporal memory layers for durable retrieval.
actual_capabilities: Explains layered agent memory architectures from working memory to permanent storage.
Compares vector stores, knowledge graphs, and temporal knowledge graphs for retrieval needs.
Provides Python reference patterns for vector search, property graphs, temporal relationships, and consolidation.
Guides entity-based and time-based memory retrieval design.
Describes consolidation and context integration practices for growing memory stores.
limitations: Provides reference patterns, not a production database or managed service.
Example embeddings use placeholder random vectors and need replacement with a real model.
Does not implement privacy consent, encryption, retention, or access control controls.
Requires adaptation for scale, reliability, backups, and database-specific query languages.

use_cases.title: Design Persistent Agent Memory
use_cases.description: Plan how an assistant should remember facts, preferences, and task state across sessions.

use_cases.title: Select Storage Architecture
use_cases.description: Compare file memory, vector retrieval, graph storage, and temporal graphs for a planned system.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Temporal Retrieval
use_cases.description: Model facts that change over time and design queries for historical state reconstruction.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Memory Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building an agent that needs memory across sessions. Compare file memory, vector search, knowledge graphs, and temporal graphs for my use case.

prompt_templates.title: Design Entity Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an entity memory model for an assistant that tracks people, projects, preferences, and relationships over multiple conversations.

prompt_templates.title: Add Temporal Retrieval
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me extend an existing memory system so facts have valid-from and valid-until dates, with retrieval for a specific historical time.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Memory System
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my agent memory architecture for retrieval quality, stale facts, consolidation strategy, privacy controls, and context integration risks.

output_examples.input: I need a support assistant to remember customer preferences across sessions.
output: Recommended design: use entity memory for each customer and store preferences as timestamped facts.
Add vector retrieval for support history and graph relationships for products, accounts, and issues.
Use retention, consent, and access controls before storing personal details.

output_examples.input: My agent must answer what a user believed or preferred last month.
output: Recommended design: use a temporal knowledge graph with validity ranges on facts.
Queries should filter facts by the requested time and exclude newer replacements.
Consolidation should preserve history instead of overwriting every older fact.

output_examples.input: Our vector memory returns related text but misses relationships between entities.
output: Recommended design: keep vector search for recall and add graph edges for relationship reasoning.
Index entities separately so retrieval can combine semantic matches with direct graph traversal.

best_practices: Match the memory architecture to the questions the agent must answer.
Store validity periods, source, and confidence when facts can change.
Add explicit privacy, consent, retention, and access controls for persistent memory.
anti_patterns: Using vector search alone when the agent must reason over relationships.
Keeping outdated facts active without temporal validity or consolidation.
Injecting all remembered data into context instead of retrieving targeted memories.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design persistent memory for agents, including vector stores, entity memory, graphs, and temporal retrieval.

faq.question: Does it provide production-ready storage?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and reference patterns that need production hardening.

faq.question: When should I use a knowledge graph?
faq.answer: Use a graph when the agent must reason about relationships between people, objects, projects, or events.

faq.question: When should I use temporal memory?
faq.answer: Use temporal memory when facts change and the agent must answer questions about past or current state.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance can be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when designing agent memory systems.

faq.question: What security controls should I add?
faq.answer: Add consent, retention limits, encryption, access control, audit logs, and deletion workflows for personal or sensitive memory.
